Unified tool catalog:
The tools listed below are available in this environment, but their schemas may be omitted from the current tool list to save context. The list is unified (native tools, MCP server tools, and tools from third-party connectors the user has connected); load and call them all the same way.
Load a listed tool with ToolSearch: pass query "select:<name>[,<name>...]" with the exact names listed below, or pass keywords (e.g. "linear issue") that match words in tool names and auto-load the best matches.
The list can grow mid-session (an MCP server finishes connecting, or the user connects a third-party connector). If a tool you need is not listed yet, re-check on later turns rather than assuming it cannot exist; just do not guess names or invent namespaces that never appear here.

This list carries only the connectors the user has already connected, and the organization may offer more that are simply not connected yet. An app missing from this list therefore never means no connector exists for it: do not tell the user the app is unavailable, and do not fall back to a browser, scraping, a shell command, or a generic skill, before you have checked what the organization offers.
When the task needs data or actions from a specific third-party app or service (including a link the user pasted) and neither a listed tool, an MCP server, nor a skill dedicated to that same service already covers it, call ConnectApp with no arguments to see which connectors this organization can connect. If that app is offered, call ConnectApp with app="<slug>" to produce a connect link for the user and ask them to connect. Fall back to another route only after ConnectApp shows the app is not offered.
ConnectApp connects a connector, not an MCP server; after connection, use only the connector tools that appear in this list.

IMPORTANT: When the task matches a listed tool, load and use it rather than routing around it using Execute. Examples: FetchUrl instead of `curl/wget/gh pr view`, WebSearch instead of Execute `gh search` or scraping search engines.

content.text:
I fixed the bug in `textutils/wrap.py`, and both tests in `tests/test_wrap.py` now pass. I didn't change the tests.

The width check was off by one. It used `<`, so it only added a word when the line came out shorter than `width`, and a line that exactly filled `width` was split. For example, `"aaa bbb"` at width 7 came out as two lines. I changed the check to `<=` so a line can be exactly `width` characters long, which is what the docstring says it should allow.
